canonical_name: CyberGym: Evaluating AI Agents' Real-World Cybersecurity Capabilities at Scale (Wang, Shi, He, Cai, Zhang, Song; UC Berkeley; ICLR 2026)
metric: Vulnerability-reproduction success rate (Level 1: description + vulnerable codebase): % of the 1,507 instances where the agent's PoC crashes the pre-patch build but not the post-patch build; leaderboard requires the final-submission (single designated PoC) metric; labs report pass@1
score_at_release_system: OpenHands + Claude-3.7-Sonnet (arXiv v1: 'The most effective combination (OpenHands and Claude-3.7-Sonnet) achieves a vulnerability reproduction success rate of only 11.9%')
lineage: Built from historical OSS-Fuzz/ARVO vulnerabilities (188 projects). Paper v2 2025-10-08 (blog rdi.berkeley.edu/blog/cybergym: Sonnet 4.5 28.9% single trial, 66.7% with 30 trials), v3 2026-03-24. Same Berkeley RDI group later released ExploitGym (arXiv 2605.11086, 2026-05; exploit generation, 869 instances) and CyberGym-E2E (arXiv 2606.04460, 2026-06; end-to-end find/PoC/patch, 920 instances), all hosted on the 'Frontier AI Cybersecurity Observatory' site cybergym.io; neither is presented as a replacement of CyberGym for saturation (E2E paper motivates itself by missing end-to-end/remediation coverage). Binary-only mode added 2026-02; SUBMISSION.md (2026-07-01) adds mandatory cost reporting and the final-submission metric.
best_by_cutoff: 88.1 pass@1, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (max reasoning effort), 2026-09-10, https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (table: 'CyberGym (Pass@1) | ... | 88.1'; HF createdAt 2026-09-10). Next: GPT-5.6 Sol 84.5 (per DeepSeek table; Grok 4.7 card lists GPT-5.6 Sol (max) 83.6%), Claude Mythos 5 83.8% (2026-06-09), DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 83.3, Claude Mythos Preview 83.1% (2026-04-07).
notes: No human baseline in the paper -> criterion B, threshold 90. No documented result >=90 on the full 1,507-task split by 2026-09-30 (lab-report trajectory: Sonnet 4.5 28.9% 2025-09, Opus 4.5 50.63% 2025-11, Opus 4.6 66.6% 2026-02, Mythos Preview 83.1% 2026-04, GPT-5.5 81.8% 2026-04, Mythos 5 83.8% 2026-06, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 88.1 2026-09). Pass@k results with oracle union (e.g. Sonnet 4.5 66.7% over 30 trials) are not the standard metric and none >=90 were found. UNCERTAINTIES: (1) the official leaderboard at https://www.cybergym.io/cybergym/ is rendered by JavaScript; its data source could not be located and GitHub issue/API access was not available -> leaderboard entries (agent systems) unverified, source unreachable; (2) Google's Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber post (2026-09-02, trusted-defender-only model) reports CyberGym Pass@1 only in a chart image ('surpasses both 3.5 Flash Cyber as well as significantly larger frontier models'); the number could not be read -> if it was >=90, AB would be 2026-09. NOT C: maintainers wrote in SUBMISSION.md (commit 9d26076, 2026-07-01) 'The most capable models under unconstrained resources have nearly saturated the benchmark... future submissions are required to report cost alongside success rate' -- the benchmark is kept active with a protocol addition, no withdrawal/freeze/replacement. Anthropic (not the maintainer) dropped it: Opus 5 card 2026-07-24 'we have dropped CyberGym as an evaluation because we consider it saturated' and Mythos 5.1 card 2026-09-01 'CyberGym (which we have retired from this system card due to saturation)' -- lab statements, not C/E. FAQ (2026-07-01) warns of leakage via network access, /src/**/.git and reference PoC /tmp/poc in dynamic setups, but no public evidence that leakage affected most frontier results -> no E. Labs still reporting through 2026-09-21 (xAI Grok 4.7 80.3%) -> not abandoned.

canonical_name: FrontierCode v1.1 (Cognition): code-quality / mergeability benchmark of ~150 tasks authored by open-source maintainers; subsets Main (100) and Extended (150)
metric: Score: weighted aggregate of rubric items on a 0-100% scale (a solution failing any 'blocker' criterion scores 0); reported on Main and Extended subsets. Secondary metric: Pass rate (clears all blockers). Grading is hybrid (unit tests + LLM-rubric + manual review by Cognition researchers)
score_at_release_system: Claude Opus 5, FrontierCode 1.1 Main, mean@5 53.4% (Anthropic Opus 5 system card, 2026-07-24, the first v1.1 lab report); v1.0 launch best was Claude Opus 4.8 Extended Score 51.8% (2026-06-08)
lineage: FrontierCode v1.0 launched 2026-06-08 (150 tasks; nested subsets Diamond 50 / Main 100 / Extended 150; crafted by 20+ open-source maintainers, '40+ hours per task'; private by design). v1.1 (2026-07-07): audited all 1000+ grading criteria and demoted 75 overly restrictive blockers, added fair/unfair internet-use detection, DEPRECATED the Diamond subset (kept Main 100 + Extended 150); 'the relative performances of the models we evaluated did not substantially change compared to 1.0' though absolute scores shifted. Coded v1.1 (8 of 10 lab reports cite v1.1). No successor by 2026-09-30.
best_by_cutoff: Extended Score 64.5%, GPT-6 Astra, 2026-09-03 (https://openai.com/index/gpt-6-astra/). Next: Claude Mythos 5.1 Extended 63.6% (2026-09-01), Grok 4.6 Extended 61.3% (2026-08-12). Main Score best: Claude Opus 5.5 54.4% (2026-09-22).
notes: No human baseline score (maintainers authored tasks but no human solve-rate reported) -> criterion B, threshold 90 on the Score metric. All results by 2026-09-30 are <=64.5% (Extended) and <=54.4% (Main), far below 90 -> alive. Dual subsets Main/Extended are nested difficulty tiers of one benchmark, not separate domains; the full set is Extended (150) so n_items=150 and best_by_cutoff uses the Extended Score; Main noted separately. v1.0 reports: Claude Mythos 5 Diamond/Main 29.3%/46.3% (2026-06-09), Claude Sonnet 5 'FrontierCode v1' 38.8% (2026-06-30). No C: v1->v1.1 is a grading-protocol refinement with relative order unchanged and explicitly not motivated by saturation; the Diamond subset was deprecated for noise, not saturation, and v1.1 itself is not deprecated. Private test set reduces contamination risk; no leakage/audit evidence -> no E. Actively evaluated through 2026-09-28 -> not abandoned.
